doc.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019

title: Letterman rehearsals: seven minutes and a circled script
summary: A daily rehearsal ran seven to nine minutes from guest-based script notes, such as circling 'Gifts A', with millions watching and little prep.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well the things you’re talking about, the hang and all that, you must have been doing when you were on the Letterman band. Maybe not consciously.
You’ve got to ask somebody else that. I’m just me. I don’t know.
Was it a high pressure gig?
So did you have like a run through in the afternoon if you were going to have musical guests?

We usually got there at like 3:45 and then we would do rehearsal. We would get a script and it would say Alec Baldwin is the first guest. And they’d say okay. We would rehearse for the show and our — I did it for 17 years, Willie did it for 30 years, Paul was 30 years, Anton — I think it was Steve Jordan then Anton, so Anton was 20 something years. These guys don’t want to rehearse. You know what I mean? So our rehearsals ran seven to nine minutes. That’s how long the rehearsal was every day. So you had a script and it was like Alec Baldwin is on the show. You’re like okay Alec Baldwin, and Alec Baldwin likes classical music. Okay let’s play “Simple Gifts” by Aaron Copland. Okay. It’s a trumpet lead and let’s put it in the key of A. Okay. So I would write Simple Gifts Trumpet A. Or I would write Gifts A and then I’d circle it and that was me.
No one wrote out a chart in other words.

No. Well sometimes we had charts. Sometimes we did. And then we’d do okay what was the top ten list. The top ten list has something to do with balloons. Okay we’ll do “99 Luftballoons” by that German band. Okay we got that. And then we got “Rockin’ Robin” © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

for Robin Williams. Okay. And then you go and you do the rehearsal and it’s like seven minutes and then the comedy does their rehearsal and then the feature band that’s on they do their rehearsal. Then they load the audience in and the comic comes on so it’s about an hour and a half, maybe two hours from the time you had your seven minute rehearsal to the show. And then the lights come on, “Daaavid Letterman” and they’re like, “Yaaay, okay.” And David Letterman goes, “And our first guest tonight is one of the Baldwin brothers.” And I’m looking at the script and it says, “Gifts A” and it’s circled. And I have no idea what that means. And there’s about, I think we had 4.7 to about 7 million people was our thing, watching, every night and it was like I don’t know what that means. That’s a high pressure gig right there. And your mind’s going — I’d better get it. And most of the time, 90% of the time you got it. When you didn’t you learned the art of I don’t know what I’m doing but it sounds like I know what I’m doing. You know? So yeah, that’s the kind of gig it was.
